extracted.intended_audience: UKRI Board members, Council members, senior UKRI executives, DSIT sponsor officials and others responsible for governance, finance, appointments and oversight of UKRI
extracted.subtask_description: A formal governance framework setting standards and requirements for UKRI-DSIT relations, board and council composition and review, appointments, financial delegations, procurement, risk, staff management, reporting and related corporate arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Board and Committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board, Councils, Executive Committee and their immediate sub-committees should be evaluated internally on an annual basis, and there should be independent input at least once every 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should be in line with any guidance issued by DSIT or other public sector guidance (including 'Corporate Governance in Central Government Departments: Code of Good Practice' and its Guidance Note). Reviews should include the Board, its committees and its individual members, and be incorporated in normal line management appraisals of executive Board members and any other appraisal processes for Board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and use of review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: These reviews should be coordinated by the relevant secretariat in consultation with the Chair (and for Councils with the Senior Independent Member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outcome of these reviews should inform the annual governance statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Governance Code for regulated public appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: For all regulated public appointments, the 'Governance Code' must be adhered to and DSIT is subject to periodic audit by the Commissioner for these appointments to ensure compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of regulated public appointments is maintained in the 'Public Appointments Order in Council' and updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSIT responsibility for ministerial appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: DSIT is accountable for making ministerial appointments to UKRI in an efficient and effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT welcomes a minimum of 12 months’ notice where possible for re-appointment recommendations and will aim to make reappointment decisions in good time to support recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSIT role in appointment process and remuneration advice
rubrics_metrics.description: DSIT will advise the Secretary of State on all public appointments to UKRI and manage the process in accordance with the Governance Code and provisions of the HER Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes advice on role specifications, remuneration, composition of recruitment panels, and advice on guidance or regulations relating to remuneration, with DSIT remaining responsible and accountable for advising ministers on elements of remuneration packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI input to appointments and agreed working with Nominations Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will provide advice and recommendations to DSIT on remuneration for ministerial appointees and will work with DSIT on the public appointments process in a timely, efficient and effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT will take into consideration advice and recommendations from UKRI when seeking ministerial and cross-government approvals through an agreed way of working with the Nominations and Remuneration Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the UKRI Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State will appoint the UKRI Chair, CEO, CFO, and at least 9 but no more than 12 other independent Board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFO will be an executive and voting Board member and appropriately qualified as a finance director (see Managing Public Money Annex 4.1). In appointing the Board the Secretary of State will take account of diverse needs (HER Act Schedule 9) so the Board members between them have experience across UKRI’s portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARAC Chair and term lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: One independent member of the Board will be appointed to take up the role of Chair of the ARAC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent members typically serve terms between 2-4 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of UKRI Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: Each UKRI Council will consist of between 5 and 12 independent members and an Executive Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Chairs appointed by the Secretary of State; independent members appointed by the Board on the recommendation of the relevant Executive Chair. Secretary of State may appoint one member to each Council. Government officials (e.g., CSAs) may attend on a personal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Chairs recruitment and timescales
rubrics_metrics.description: The UKRI CEO will lead on recruitment campaigns for Council Executive Chairs, with Ministers ratifying the panel’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSIT officials and Ministers will support recruitment exercises in no less than 90 days from campaign materials submission to Ministers to the point an offer is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance management of ministerial appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministerial appointees to UKRI should be subject to annual performance appraisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director General (DSIT Science, Innovation & Growth) arranges appraisal of the UKRI Chair representing views of DSIT ministers and Permanent Secretary. UKRI Chair responsible for performance management of CEO and CFO (may delegate CFO appraisal to CEO, liaising with DSIT). CEO responsible for performance management of Council Executive Chairs, liaising with DSIT. UKRI performance management should align with DSIT guidance for appraisal of independent and executive leaders; significant variances discussed and agreed in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic presumption of reappointment
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no automatic presumption of reappointment for public appointees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers will make reappointment decisions based on merit and will not agree reappointment/extension without written evidence of satisfactory performance appraisal (Governance Code on Public Appointments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Devolution: remit and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI has a UK‑wide remit for certain councils and Innovate UK; Research England’s primary focus is English higher education providers, but it should cooperate with devolved counterparts where efficient and effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research England may carry out UK‑wide activity if authorised by the UKRI Board. In decisions with significant impact on higher education providers, UKRI should draw on information from Research England, Office for Students or relevant devolved bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with devolved administrations
rubrics_metrics.description: DSIT will regularly engage with the devolved administrations on UKRI’s priorities, including working with devolved funding bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement includes working through the UK Funders of Research and Innovation Group; UKRI will engage closely with devolved funding bodies but decisions on reserved matters remain with UKRI and UK ministers. Consider security and risk when transferring information between devolved authorities and central government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint working with the Office for Students
rubrics_metrics.description: HER Act provides for joint working between UKRI and the Office for Students and places duties to reflect collaborative approach between research and teaching agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collaboration agreement will set out formal structures for engagement and information sharing, including consultation on priorities for investing HEIF teaching element and alignment of governance arrangements via DSIT and Department for Education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with other bodies in the research and innovation landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI should work closely and collaboratively with other bodies on areas of shared interest to maximise benefits to research and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine collaboration and coordination to support implementation of programmes and provision of expert advice to government priorities; monitor such engagement centrally and provide updates to DSIT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangements where UKRI delivers DSIT programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: When UKRI is asked to deliver programmes on behalf of DSIT (where DSIT responsible for budgets and funding decisions), roles, responsibilities and resourcing should be discussed and agreed in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These arrangements will be reviewed and adjusted as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with other government departments
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will engage with other government departments as a matter of routine and play a central role in enabling Government's strategic agenda for research and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work closely to implement programmes and provide expert advice and analysis; UKRI should monitor engagement centrally and provide DSIT updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegated authorities documentation and review
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI’s delegated authorities are set out in the delegation letter and will be communicated to the UKRI CEO as Accounting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation letters may be updated and superseded by DSIT in agreement with HM Treasury. Delegations will be reviewed annually in line with Managing Public Money Annex 2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior written approval for out-of-delegation actions
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall obtain DSIT’s and, where appropriate, HM Treasury’s prior written approval before undertaking specified activities outside delegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities requiring approval include entering into expenditure outside delegations or budget, incurring novel/contentious expenditure, making significant changes in scale of operation or funding of previously approved initiatives, making policy or practice changes with wider financial implications, and carrying out policies contrary to Managing Public Money principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and handling of 'novel and contentious' activities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal definition of 'novel and contentious'; Managing Public Money provides guidance and interpretation should involve early engagement with the DSIT sponsor team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel may be activity new to UKRI or without easy comparators; contentious may raise concerns about Accounting Officer standards (regularity, propriety, value for money, feasibility). Novel/contentious activities require careful consideration and escalation to DSIT and HM Treasury and an Accounting Officer assessment where concerns arise. Examples include dual use research of concern and novel administrative/legal structures. All proposals and existing activity should be periodically assessed for appropriateness and ability to withstand public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: UK Shared Business Services (UK SBS) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: UK SBS is a company wholly owned by its public sector customers and is a recognised government Shared Service provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI may use UK SBS for transactional and specialist services to support effective corporate service delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spending authority and compliance with Managing Public Money
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless agreed by DSIT and HM Treasury, UKRI shall follow Managing Public Money principles and can incur budget-approved expenditure without further reference to DSIT subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include complying with delegation letter, Managing Public Money regarding VfM/feasibility/regularity/propriety, seeking DSIT/HM Treasury agreement for establishing subsidiaries (considered 'novel'), and providing sponsor department with requested operational/performance/expenditure information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banking and cash management
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI must maximise use of publicly procured banking services (Government Banking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI should only hold money outside Government Banking Service where a good business case exists and HM Treasury consent is required for each account. Commercial accounts must be with members of relevant UK clearing bodies and operated in line with Managing Public Money principles. The Accounting Officer is responsible for ensuring UKRI has a banking policy and that it is complied with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement policy and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall ensure procurement policies align with UK/international procurement rules, in particular the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, and document policies in a Procurement Policy and Procedures Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where procurement likely exceeds delegated authority, procurement strategy approval must be sought from sponsor team. Procurement should be by competition; single-tender or restricted contracts should be limited and exceptional with quarterly reporting of exceptions to DSIT. Procurement decisions should be based on a full option appraisal and value for money (optimum combination of whole life costs and quality). UKRI shall engage with government procurement initiatives, comply with Procurement Policy Notes, and cooperate to improve procurement data availability. UKRI shall comply with commercial and grants standards for government commercial activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall ensure that risks it faces are dealt with appropriately in accordance with best practice and develop a risk management strategy per Treasury guidance 'Management of Risk: Principles and Concepts'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI must inform DSIT at the earliest appropriate time of significant emerging issues and risks, align risk management with Managing Public Money and DSIT policies/systems, establish processes to capture/escalate/communicate risks, and monitor/report major projects and major operational/financial/reputational risks on a schedule agreed with DSIT. Cyber security robustness should be proportionate to size and risk exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter fraud, theft and propriety measures
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI should adopt and implement policies and practices to safeguard against fraud and theft and act in line with Counter Fraud Function guidance and Managing Public Money annexes and the Counter Fraud Functional Standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records and prepare/forward annual reports on fraud/theft to DSIT; notify sponsor department of unusual/major incidents promptly; report detected losses and recoveries to the counter fraud centre in line with government definitions; maintain a register of interests for Board and Council members published annually; establish and publish a gift and hospitality policy; maintain records of entertainment given/received; be mindful of public perceptions around appropriate use of public money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff recruitment and broad responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Within arrangements approved by the responsible Minister and Treasury, UKRI will have responsibility for recruitment, retention and motivation of staff and ensure rules create an inclusive culture with merit-based appointment and advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate staffing levels and structure for economy, efficiency and effectiveness; satisfactory appraisal of performance at all levels; encourage professional and management expertise; proper consultation on key issues; adequate grievance and disciplinary procedures; whistle-blowing procedures consistent with Public Interest Disclosure Act; code of conduct based on Cabinet Office Model Code for Executive NDPB staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of staff costs and creation of posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to delegated authorities, UKRI shall ensure creation of any additional posts does not incur forward commitments exceeding its ability to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI must manage staffing levels within approved budgets and delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay and conditions of service compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI staff are subject to levels of remuneration and terms and conditions within the general pay structure approved by DSIT and the Treasury and must comply with public sector pay policy and guidance applicable to NDPBs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI is subject to an annual pay remit process agreed by DSIT and HMT; must comply with Treasury guidance on senior salaries and performance pay; UKRI has no delegated power to amend these terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Civil Service terms where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: If civil service terms and conditions apply to pay/allowances, payment shall be made in accordance with the Civil Service Management Code and annual Civil Service Pay Remit Guidance unless DSIT gives prior approval to vary rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures alignment with civil service pay frameworks where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior pay controls and approval thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific pay controls for senior UKRI staff are set by Government to ensure appropriate senior pay while ensuring value for money; Guidance for Approval of Senior Pay sets process for approving remuneration packages over a designated value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Chief Secretary to the Treasury (CST) approval not required, sponsoring departments must undertake a value for money assessment; DSIT has set thresholds for Partner Organisations and remuneration packages above threshold must receive DSIT approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee handbook requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff terms and conditions should be set out in an Employee Handbook which should be provided to the department together with subsequent amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures DSIT is sighted on staff terms and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-related pay scheme operation
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI shall operate a performance-related pay scheme that shall form part of the annual aggregate pay budget approved by DSIT where relevant with due regard to Senior Pay Guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance pay must be managed within DSIT-approved budgetary and guidance constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board members’ travel expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The travel expenses of Board members shall be tied to the rates allowed to senior staff of UKRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable actual costs shall be reimbursed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pensions, redundancy and compensation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation scheme rules and pension scheme rules should reflect legislative and HM Treasury guidance regarding exit payments; staff shall normally be eligible for Civil Service Pension Scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to change pension arrangements or to pay redundancy/compensation require prior DSIT approval; redundancy payments must follow Civil Service Compensation Scheme; severance proposals must comply with Managing Public Money (chapter 4). Employers’ contributions to personal pensions normally limited to national insurance rebate level; MRC Institute staff access Medical Research Pension scheme where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate and business plans and UKRI Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State may commission a research and innovation strategy ('The UKRI Strategy'); the Board will oversee development and the Secretary of State will approve the Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will engage on critical challenges/policy context; councils will produce strategic delivery plans covering Spending Review periods that set out how each Council will exercise functions and prioritise budgets. Strategic delivery plans submitted to the Board for approval and once agreed provide mechanisms for delegation of functions under the HER Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate plan development and content
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will develop a corporate plan setting out how it will deliver against the UKRI Strategy and statutory duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will agree issues and timetable with DSIT; the plan will demonstrate contribution to DSIT medium-term plan and include size/structure/costs/benefits. The corporate plan will be updated annually with key targets/milestones linked to budgeting so resources for objectives can be identified. Matters to include: important objectives and associated key performance targets; strategy for operational expenditure efficiency; key non-financial performance targets; context of risk factors; and other matters agreed between DSIT and UKRI. Performance framework should report delivery progress against corporate plan targets. UKRI will submit plan/updates to DSIT for agreement and Secretary of State will approve each corporate plan or update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget allocations, advice and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State will make budget allocations for UKRI and each Council, taking advice from the Board on strategic priorities and funding balance between disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board should consider the wider landscape when advising and consult relevant bodies to reflect expertise and interests. DSIT may invite the Board to provide advice on other funding matters relevant to research and innovation landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting procedures and DSIT grant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year DSIT will send UKRI a formal statement (grant/allocation letter) of annual budgetary provision and any planned policy changes affecting UKRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making grants to UKRI the Secretary of State may provide terms and conditions and will have regard to Haldane principle, balanced funding principle and any Board advice. Corporate plan should take account of approved funding and forecast receipts and include profile of expected expenditure and draw-down of departmental funding. DSIT reserves right to vary UKRI funding in exceptional circumstances (e.g., emergency budget or systemic contravention of Accounting Officer duty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting and reporting cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will operate on a multi-year cycle for strategy, budgeting and delivery kept live through annual adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board responsible for preparing annual report and accounts each financial year and will engage with DSIT on the DSIT 'Single Departmental Plan'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-in-aid and ring-fenced grant management
rubrics_metrics.description: Any grant-in-aid will be voted in the department’s Supply Estimate and be subject to parliamentary control; grant-in-aid normally paid monthly on basis of written applications showing evidence of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No payment in advance of need; cash balances kept to minimum consistent with efficient operation; unspent grant-in-aid lapses at year end (subject to parliamentary approval for carry-forward exceptions); DSIT will provide funding next year if required to meet year-end liabilities; ring-fenced grants issued per agreed business case profiles and require evidence funds used for authorised purposes; UKRI shall not hold uncommitted grant funds or carry grant funds over to another financial year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report and accounts requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The UKRI Board must publish an annual report of activities together with audited accounts after each financial year and provide finalised accounts to DSIT by a date notified each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft report should be submitted to DSIT before publication. Accounts prepared in accordance with relevant statutes, accounts direction and the Treasury's Financial Reporting Manual (FReM). The annual report must cover any corporate/subsidiary/joint ventures under control, comply with FReM (illustrative statements for an NDPB), outline main activities and performance against strategic objectives (with comparable outturns where appropriate), set out key elements of Councils' activities/expenditure in summary form, include forward plans, include a statement on cooperation with the Office for Students and on international collaboration. Performance against key financial targets is included and subject to the auditor's consistency opinion. The report and accounts shall be laid in Parliament and made available on the UKRI website. Timeframes for draft submission and Secretary of State approval agreed with DSIT sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting performance to the department
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI will operate management, information and accounting systems enabling timely and effective review of financial and non-financial performance against budgets and corporate targets, and share this information with DSIT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will inform DSIT of any changes affecting achievement of objectives, report performance including in helping to deliver Ministers’ policies according to an agreed schedule, and be formally reviewed by DSIT quarterly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sharing obligations (introductory)
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI must operate information sharing arrangements with DSIT and other partners (section begins here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details in following sections (not included in this chunk) — indicates obligation to share management, operational and assurance information with DSIT and partners as agreed.
